result.summary: Removes time-based mempool transaction eviction (`-mempoolexpiry`) and its associated multi_index container index. Transactions now only leave the mempool via block inclusion, replacement, conflict, or size-based eviction under `-maxmempool`. The configuration option `-mempoolexpiry` is retained as a hidden no-op option that issues a warning when set.
result.problem: Evicting transactions purely based on age (previously defaulting to two weeks) drops transactions that remain incentive-compatible and mineable, such as low-feerate parents waiting on CPFP fee-bumping children. Maintaining the age-based index also imposes per-entry memory overhead for an eviction mechanism that conflicts with miner incentives.
evidence: Fixes linked issue #33510 ('Mempool Expiry eviction might remove txs that could be mined in the next block')
Author description and commit message note eviction by age is incentive-incompatible and can drop still-mineable transactions waiting on child fee bumps
Author description highlights secondary memory savings: 'removing it saves an ordered-tree node per mempool entry... within the same -maxmempool budget the mempool fits slightly more transactions'
result.scope_notes: Touches mempool eviction logic, removes the `entry_time` index from CTxMempool's multi_index, removes the `EXPIRY` removal reason, updates fuzz and unit tests to stop expecting expiry, and keeps `-mempoolexpiry` as a deprecated hidden CLI argument.
result.card: Removes time-based transaction expiry (-mempoolexpiry) and deletes the mempool entry_time index. Evicting transactions by elapsed time can drop mineable transactions that may still be confirmed, such as low-feerate transactions with fee-bumping children, contradicting miner incentives. Eliminating the index also reduces memory usage per mempool entry. Transactions will now only leave the mempool via block inclusion, RBF/conflicts, or size-based eviction (-maxmempool).

risk.why: A flaw in mempool eviction or index removal could alter transaction retention policies or cause memory management bugs across mempool entries.
